rows.title: One link, one thing
rows.body: A link points at exactly what you chose: a date range, your live position, a single track, a trip, a month of statistics, or a yearly digest. Sharing last weekend's ride tells the person nothing about last Tuesday.

rows.title: Everything the link does is decided before you send it
rows.body: A phrase is generated for you and can be cleared if you would rather not use one. The expiry defaults to a week out and can be blanked for a link that never expires. Photos start switched off, so you will never send a page and find out afterwards that it showed more than you meant.
rows.note: Off by default, on by decision

objections.q: Does sharing a link expose my whole history?
objections.a: No. A link resolves to the one resource it was created for. A timeline link is bounded by the dates you picked; a track link shows that track. There is no path from a shared page to the rest of your account.

objections.q: What if I send it to the wrong person?
objections.a: Revoke it. The link stops resolving straight away. If you had set a passphrase, you can instead regenerate just the phrase, which invalidates every unlock anyone has already done while keeping the link itself alive.

objections.q: Do the people I share with need an account?
objections.a: No. A shared page opens in any browser. If you set a passphrase they enter that, and nothing else.

objections.q: Can I see whether anyone opened it?
objections.a: Yes. Live location, date-range, trip and track links show how many times they have been opened and when they were last viewed, and all of them are listed together in one place.

objections.q: What happens to my links if my subscription expires?
objections.a: You can export everything at any time, and the whole application is open source — you can run the same features on your own hardware for free, permanently.
